In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the studied IL is a promising solvent for N 3 O capture and that the soft-SAFT Eo S can be used to accurately predict gas solubility and selectivity in ILs.
the ILs are promising candidates for CO 2 capture and separation processes, however the development of ILs with high CO 2 selectivity and low viscosity still represents an important challenge.
ILs with high molar volumes, and therefore low densities, are not suitable as a solvent for the capture of GHGs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the solubility behavior of N 2, CH 4 and CO 2 in ILs are very different, and the ILs with the highest CO 2 selectivity are not the ones that present the highest selectivity towards N 2 or N 2 O.
the studied ionic liquid is a promising solvent to separate N 2 from CH 4 or N 2 O at low temperatures, but its application for the separation of N 2 from N 2 O or CH 4 is not recommended.

ILs with low polarity and high molar volume are not suitable for N 2 capture and that ILs with high polarity and low molar volume are more appropriate for CO 2 and N 2 O capture, whereas for CH 4 separation, ILs with high molar volume and moderate polarity are preferred.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the IL [C 4 mC 1 im][DCA] is not a good candidate for the capture of N 2 O or for the separation of N 2 /CH 4.
the IL [C 4 m im][N(CCN) 2 ] has an unfavorable behavior for the separation of N 2 O from CH 4, and for N 2 and CH 4 from each other.

the solubility behavior of gases in [C 3 C 1 im + ][N(CN)2] can be predicted with a high accuracy, which is a valuable information for the design and development of IL based membranes for gas separation.
